stemBlocks.value: On a square grid, triangle X'Y'Z' has vertices X'(−3, 7), Y'(−1, 7) and Z'(−3, 3), and triangle X"Y"Z" has vertices X"(7, 7), Y"(5, 7) and Z"(7, 3). (i) Triangle X'Y'Z' is the image of triangle XYZ after an enlargement of scale factor 2 with centre (5, 1) — draw the object triangle XYZ on the grid. (ii) Triangle X'Y'Z' is mapped onto X"Y"Z" by a reflection in the line P; state the equation of the mirror line P.
Think first: To undo an enlargement of scale factor 2, halve each point's distance from the centre instead of doubling it.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p258-q17 from workbook page 258.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the inverse of the enlargement about (5, 1) with scale factor 2.

contentBlocks.value: If image = C + 2(object − C), then object = C + (image − C)/2

solutionSteps.instruction: Apply it to each vertex of X'Y'Z'.
Check the enlargement forwards on one vertex.

contentBlocks.value: From (5, 1) to X(1, 4) is (−4, 3); doubling gives (−8, 6), landing on (−3, 7) = X' ✓

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the mirror line by taking the midpoint of a point and its image.

contentBlocks.value: X'(−3, 7) and X"(7, 7): midpoint x = (−3 + 7)/2 = 2; Y'(−1, 7) and Y"(5, 7): midpoint x = 2; y-coordinates are unchanged, so the mirror is vertical

strategyBlocks.value: Apply the inverse rule object = centre + (image − centre) ÷ 2 to each vertex of X'Y'Z', then find the mirror line as the vertical line midway between corresponding points of the two triangles.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) Triangle XYZ has vertices X(1, 4), Y(2, 4) and Z(1, 2) — half the size of X'Y'Z' and drawn between it and the centre (5, 1).  (ii) The mirror line P is x = 2.

whyThisWorks.value: An enlargement of scale factor 2 puts every image point twice as far from the centre as its object, so reversing it means halving that displacement — which is exactly an enlargement of scale factor 1/2 about the same centre. A reflection leaves every point at the same perpendicular distance from the mirror on the opposite side, so the mirror passes through the midpoint of each point and its image; because only the x-coordinates change here, that mirror is a vertical line.

commonErrors.misconception: Halving the coordinates themselves rather than the distances from the centre (5, 1).

examTip.value: Always express a mirror line as an equation (x = a, y = b, y = x or y = −x) — a description in words rarely scores full marks.
